sections.reference_shloka:
विष हिंगुल मंजिष्ठा हरिताल मनःशिला। 
धनसारत्रयी तुत्थद्वय गन्धक नाकुली ।। 
श्रीवेष्टक सर्जरस गौरीयष्ट्याहव गोपिकाः। 
नवसार वरा दारु कुन्दुरुष्क निशाद्वयैः।। 
चिंचाफलास्थि स्थौणेय मेषविष्ठा जपात्वचः। 
शाकनिम्ब कपित्थाप्रनिर्यास कूहलीरपि।। 
क्षीरेण वटवृक्षस्य शल्मलीत्वग्रसेन वा। 
प्रत्यग्रकेरमद्येन कुक्कुटाण्डद्रवेण वा।। 
पिष्ट्वा सम्यक्समालिप्य वासखण्डैघनीयसि। 
ब्राधिष्टेऽथ च संवेष्ट्य शलाकां लोहनिर्मिताम् ।। 
शोषयित्वा पुराणाज्यसिक्तां दीपयेत्पुनः । 
एकत्र तिलकेरोत्थस्नेही कृत्वा समांशकौ।। 
दीप्यमानां शलाकां तां तस्योपरि च धारयेत्। 
अवागग्रां मुहुः सिंचन् ताभ्यामन्यत्र पातयेत् ।। 
शलाकाग्रगतान् स्नेहविन्दूना स्नेहसंस्रयात् । दीप्यमानाच्छलाकाग्रान्पात्रे पतितमादरात् ।। 
आदाय तैलं सत्पात्रे निषिच्य परिपालयेत्। 
संप्राप्तेवासरे तेन लेपनं विदधीत च।। 
व्रणभैरवनामेदं तैलं मत्र्येन दुर्लभम्। 
असितेनपुरा दुष्टव्रणार्त वीक्ष्य बालकम् ।। 
यमिना सत्कृतेनोक्तं गृहस्थायाग्निशर्मणे। सर्वव्रणहरं सद्यः किंचिद् संनिपातजित् ।। 
असाध्येष्वपि सिद्धेच्च विसपांदिषु च ध्रुवम्। 
सर्वेषु वातरोगेषु वाताचे चापराजितम् ।। 
उन्मादे चाप्यपस्मारे लेपनस्यादिकर्मभिः। 
भेलेन तपसा तैलमेतल्लब्धमनिन्दित्तम् ।। 
तन्मुखात्केचनाविदन्मन्ये केचित्तदागमात् ।। (Sahasrayogam) 

 The verse explains that mineral and herbal substances are triturated, processed through heating, and the medicated oil collected for therapeutic application in severe conditions, particularly wounds and tridosha disorders.

 Sariba (Hemidesmus indicus – Indian Sarsaparilla) – 10 g

 Haritaki (Terminalia chebula – Chebulic Myrobalan) – 10 g

 Amalaki (Emblica officinalis – Indian Gooseberry) – 10 g 
 Devadaru (Cedrus deodara – Himalayan Cedar) – 10 g 
 Kundurushka (Boswellia serrata – Indian Frankincense) – 10 g

 Daruharidra (Berberis aristata – Tree Turmeric) – 10 g 
 Chincha Phala Asthi (Tamarindus indica – Tamarind Seed) – 10 g 
 Sthauneya (Clerodendrum phlomidis – Arni) – 10 g 
 Mesa Vishta (Ovis aries – Processed Sheep Dung) – 10 g 
 Japa Tvak (Hibiscus rosa-sinensis – Hibiscus Bark) – 10 g 
 Nimba (Azadirachta indica – Neem) – 10 g 
 Kapittha (Limonia acidissima – Wood Apple) – 10 g 
 Amra Niryasa (Mangifera indica – Mango Resin) – 10 g 

 II. Mardana Dravyas (Grinding Media) 

 Vata Kshira (Ficus benghalensis – Banyan Latex) 
 Shalmali Tvak Rasa (Bombax ceiba – Silk Cotton Bark Juice) 
 Fresh Coconut Fermented Liquid 
 Kukkutanda Drava (Hen’s Egg Liquid) 

 III. Taila Dravyas 

 Tila Taila (Sesamum indicum – Sesame Oil) – 640 ml 
 Narikela Taila (Cocos nucifera – Coconut Oil) – 640 ml 

 Method Of Preparation 
 All ingredients are purified where required and powdered separately. The powders are triturated thoroughly using the prescribed grinding media until a smooth homogeneous paste is obtained. The prepared paste is applied uniformly over a clean cloth, which is wrapped firmly around an iron rod and allowed to dry completely. After drying, the material is coated with cow’s ghee and subjected to controlled heating. During heating, medicated oil droplets are released from the preparation. These droplets are carefully collected in a vessel containing a mixture of sesame oil and coconut oil. The collected oil is filtered and stored in clean airtight containers. This specialized transformation process yields Vranabhairava Taila. 
 Method Of Use 

 External application over affected areas. 
 Therapeutic oil massage (Abhyanga). 
 Nasal administration (Nasya) under professional supervision.

Wound cleansing and healing support 
 Anti-inflammatory and tissue stabilizing effect 
 Tridosha pacifying with emphasis on Vata control 
 Penetrative and detoxifying action 
 Supportive in chronic pathological conditions 

 Clinical Indications 

 Chronic and non-healing wounds 
 Infected ulcers and inflammatory lesions 
 Sannipata disorders 
 Visarpa (spreading inflammatory condition) 
 Vata Vyadhi (neuromuscular disorders) 
 Vatarakta (Gout-like disorder) 
 Unmada (psychological disturbances) 
 Apasmara (seizure disorders)
sections.precautions:
This formulation contains potent mineral components and should be used only under supervision of a qualified Ayurvedic practitioner. Intended primarily for external therapeutic use. Store in airtight containers away from heat and moisture. 
 Conclusion 
 Vranabhairava Taila is a classical Ayurvedic medicated oil obtained through a specialized process integrating purified minerals, herbal substances, and resinous compounds into an oil medium. The formulation is traditionally valued for its potency in chronic wounds, inflammatory disorders, and severe Vata-dominant conditions. When prepared according to classical procedure and applied appropriately, it functions as a powerful external therapeutic preparation in Ayurvedic practice.

 Introduction 
 Vranabhairava Taila is a classical Ayurvedic medicated oil prepared through a specialized transformation process involving purified minerals, herbal drugs, and resinous substances integrated into an oil base. The method of preparation is distinctive, involving trituration with specific liquid media, controlled heating, and collection of medicated oil through a transformation process. Due to its complex composition and method, the oil is considered highly powerful and is employed under expert supervision in classical practice.
